headline: Losses narrow but tariffs keep squeezing gross margin
summary_short: Under Armour's fiscal Q4 revenue was $1,171.2M, down 0.8% y/y, as gross margin fell to 42.0% (-464bps y/y) on tariff and pricing pressure; the operating loss narrowed to $25.7M from $56.4M a year ago on lower marketing, facility and litigation-reserve costs.
summary_long: FY2026 (year ended March 31, 2026) net revenue fell 3.8% to $4,966.4M, led by a 7.9% North America decline versus EMEA (+8.6%) and Latin America (+8.7%) growth. Full-year gross margin compressed ~240bps to 45.5% on tariff costs (155bps) and unfavorable pricing (70bps). Fiscal Q4 (the reported quarter) revenue was $1,171.2M, -0.8% y/y, with gross margin at 42.0%. Operating loss narrowed to $25.7M from $56.4M a year ago on lower marketing, facility and litigation-reserve costs, partly offset by tariffs. Cash fell to $309.2M after a $601.2M restricted deposit to discharge 2026 Senior Notes; long-term debt rose to $1,190.4M on a new $400M note. No Fiscal 2027 numeric guidance was disclosed.

drivers.explanation: Challenging market conditions persisted in North America and Asia-Pacific on lower consumer demand across wholesale and DTC channels; tariff cost increases from the IEEPA litigation further pressured margins through the year.
North America net revenue fell 7.9% on lower wholesale and DTC (e-commerce and stores) demand; EMEA (+8.6%) and Latin America (+8.7%) grew on higher wholesale and DTC sales, partially offsetting.

Full-year 240bps margin decline was driven by 155bps of tariff impact, 70bps of unfavorable pricing and 45bps of unfavorable channel/regional mix, partly offset by 45bps FX and 20bps favorable product mix.

North America operating income fell 29.7% on lower revenue and tariff-driven input costs, but Corporate Other's loss narrowed 15.8% on lower litigation reserve expense (prior year included a $261M securities-litigation settlement).
Investing cash outflows rose $562.5M as the company deposited $601.2M into a restricted investment to satisfy and discharge the Senior Notes due 2026.
The company issued $400M of Senior Notes due 2030 in June 2025 and drew on its revolving credit facility during the year to fund the Senior Notes due 2026 discharge.
